newsitem.title: MEXICO: Final Mexico election results due on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Final Mexico election results due on Thursday.

text.p: Final results from Sunday's elections in Mexico won't be issued until midday on Thursday, the Federal Electoral Institute (IFE) said on on Wednesday.
The IFE gave results Monday night from a preliminary count of 86 percent of polling stations.

This showed the ruling PRI likely to lose its majority in the lower house of Congress with a 38.8 percent share of the national vote. But the results not counted included rural areas where the PRI has traditionally enjoyed strong support.

Mexico City's Reforma newspaper estimated on Wednesday that if the tendency shown in the first 86 percent of preliminary results were maintained, the PRI would end up 13 seats short of a majority in the 500-seat Chamber of Deputies.
The Institutional Revolutionary Party also lost the Mexico City mayoral race to a left-wing opposition leader in the worst trouncing in its seven decades in power.
The IFE's governing General Council adjourned on Monday evening after giving the preliminary numbers and resumed work on Wednesday.
IFE technical secretary Felipe Solis Acero said the 300 electoral districts across the country were now working out the final figures for the congressional races.
The IFE General Council said it expected to give fresh information at 2100 Wednesday night (0200 GMT Thursday) on the final results of most of the 300 electoral districts.
But only on Thursday would final results come in, as well as the assignation of the 200 lower house deputies chosen by proportional representation.
Solis said 132 of the planned 104,716 voting booths across Mexico were not set up on election day because of problems.
Most of those (86) were in the troubled southern state of Chiapas, where Zapatista Indian rebels called on their supporters to boycott the election.

Another 28 were in the southern state of Oaxaca, which saw some pre-electoral violence mainly directed against the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD). The remainder were scattered between various other states.
Of the 104,584 booths set up, sealed urns of ballot papers and results had been received from 104,360, he added.
